name: How the draft artifacts are authored (the product-truth agents)
summary: The agent pipeline behind define-a-feature's draft step: a classifier decides which artifacts a request needs, then only the required authoring agents run — a mock-data agent drafts or extends the one canonical dataset, a mockup agent draws the screens from that data, a flow agent assembles the journey wiring steps to screens and entities, and finally the business-analyst derives the acceptance criteria from the flow's steps. The handoff medium between agents is the artifact each produces plus the classifier's decision, so a single-screen tweak never spins up a whole journey and a backend job never drafts a screen. None of these agents exist yet — this flow is the spec for building them, so every step renders not-started.

steps.label: Classify what the request needs
steps.human:
A classifier reads the plain-language request and decides which artifacts it needs — flow, mock data, mockups, or a subset — plus the target component and entities, so the pipeline only runs the agents that fit.

I/O boundary: This is the pt-classifier prompt output, not a labelled classifier-eval row. The pipeline remains a specification; this schema documents an existing prompt contract and does not prove orchestration is wired.

steps.label: Flow agent assembles the journey
steps.human:
The flow agent assembles the draft flow, ordering the steps and wiring each to its screen and the entities it reads and writes, with an acceptance_scenario per step.

I/O boundary: The draft *.flow.json is the authored contract. Examples are projections, not runnable complete flows; linked screen and AC existence is still validated against the store.

The flow author also records each real handoff using source-bound fields and coherent JSON examples, distinguishes runtime contracts from reviewed documentation or illustrative designs, and states any genuinely undefined proposed binding. Internal human/UI transitions state why there is no JSON handoff. The author then regenerates compatibility text and validates the artifact.

steps.label: Business-analyst derives the ACs
steps.human:
Once the person approves the drafted flow, the business-analyst derives the L2/L3 acceptance criteria from the flow's steps and back-links each step via step.implements — the flow stays the reviewable source of truth.

I/O boundary: The human approval is conversational; BA then writes parsed AC YAML and exact step.implements links. Metadata does not advance the real AC readiness or claim that generation already runs.
